qualification: local A05.3 reliability isolation; not A05.3 closure, performance acceptance, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

candidate.acceptedBoundary: The production PC machine permits same-tier direct chaining only within legacy baseline and optimizing compiler ABIs. Tier-one execution remains enabled, but Tier-one blocks cannot initiate raw direct links and the existing compiler-ABI gate prevents them from accepting legacy links. The generated IBTC and shadow-return stack remain absent.
candidate.behavioralIntent: Separate legacy-source direct edges from Tier-one-source direct edges after the combined direct-chain-only candidate reproduced intermittent guest corruption.
candidate.productionFinding: Two runs of the exact same hashed release runner passed all seven authenticated workloads and powered off. Both exercised legacy direct chaining while compiling Tier-one blocks, and both recorded zero IBTC and shadow-return activity. This accepts legacy-source direct chaining as a bounded production reliability boundary and narrows the remaining direct-chain suspect to Tier-one-source edges or an interaction they enable.

verification.focused: 37 tests in two suites passed: three predictor-boundary regressions plus DoryPCDirectKernelMachineTests.
verification.deterministicAggregate: 1,558 tests in 179 suites passed with test parallelism disabled.

retainedBaseline.reason: The accepted legacy-only reliability boundary intentionally excludes Tier-one direct sources, the IBTC, and shadow returns, so its 13.74-percent bypass share cannot replace the broader accepted enabled-path measurement.

disposition.reason: Production retains legacy-source direct chaining. A05.3 remains open because Tier-one direct initiation must be isolated and repaired or excluded, the remaining predictors require independent reintroduction, and the final enabled path must exceed 95-percent dispatcher avoidance.

limitations: Two passing local runs are a bounded reliability check, not cross-host qualification or proof that every intermittent failure has been eliminated.
The compiler-source split narrows the preceding direct-chain-only failure but does not identify a specific corrupting Tier-one edge or prove sole causality.
The measured 13.74-percent within-run avoidance is below the strict A05.3 performance threshold and receives no replacement credit over the accepted broader enabled-path baseline.
The raw diagnostic receipts remain in /private/tmp; this checked-in record binds their hashes and selected counters.
